articles.title: New reservoir offers innovative solution to South Sudan cattle beef
articles.summary: At the end of a history-laden path winding through palm trees and scattered ruins – remnants of once-vibrant villages destroyed by cattle raids – lies a rare sight in this dry part of Terekeka county in South Sudan: a sparkling, fresh water source.
articles.content:
The artificial lake is one of the latest outcomes of a quick impact project, initiated by the UN peacekeeping mission in South Sudan (UNMISS).

While UNMISS is mandated by the Security Council to protect civilians in restive parts of the country, part of its tasks include supporting the communities peacekeepers serve, from building roads to building peace.

Cattle conflicts

The reservoir project in Terekeka responds not only to the chronic lack of water in the area, but also to a key driver of conflict, with ongoing competition between farmers and cattle keepers over scarce water and grazing resources.

The intention was clear from the outset: provide farmers with a reliable water source for their crops while reducing the need for cattle keepers to venture onto farmland in search of water for their livestock, a perennial source of tension and violence.

“This project is particularly close to our hearts as it directly addresses both humanitarian challenges and conflict triggers, and the impact is already visible,” said UNMISS Civil Affairs Officer Lawson Assagaya at a recent ceremony handing over the reservoir to the community.

Location is key

The location was carefully chosen, far enough from farms to reduce competition, yet close enough for farming communities to benefit, UNMISS said.

The hope is that the reservoir will create new opportunities for herders and farmers to co-exist peacefully, and signs of change are already emerging.

New cattle camps have already begun to settle around the reservoir, encouraging those displaced by conflict, including members of the Wonduruba Mundari community, to begin returning home.

Brighter future

Cattle keeper John Kenyi, a father of three who is expecting his fourth child, has long hoped to see changes that would, among other things, give his children a brighter future.

“It’s devastating to see how our peaceful people end up fighting over scarce resources and lack of coordinated migration patterns rather than working together,” he said. “Every day I hope for unity to return.”

For Mr. Kenyi, cattle are not simply a status symbol, but an investment that can help pay for his children’s education, an approach he says he learned from neighbouring farming communities.

“I don’t know if I would say that we were brothers, but we are certainly one community,” he said. “It gives us pride that this county is now re-emerging as a place people can call home.”

Working together

This sense of unity also emerged during the reservoir’s construction, according to the Point Investment Company, the project’s local partner.

When workers arrived at the site, they found no road suitable for the heavy machinery needed to begin work.

As news of the project had spread, farmers and herders from surrounding communities quickly arrived with tools to help clear and build a pathway to the site.

“What was particularly special about constructing this project was the excitement of the Rego payam community,” said Point Investment Company project manager Juman Emmanuel. “You could really see how energised everyone was about this new water source.”

© UNICEF/Sebastian Rich

Boost from nature

Nature also provided an unexpected boost to the project when workers struck an underground water source that began naturally filling the roughly 3,200-square-metre reservoir.

The discovery meant the cement lining originally planned was no longer an option as it could contaminate the clean groundwater.

“When we saw the water coming out from underground, we were all relieved,” the construction workers said. “This meant that the Rego communities will have an even more sustainable opportunity to be safe now.”

Renewed hope

The project was completed in just one month, leaving the community with a sustainable water source that can continue replenishing the reservoir even when rainfall becomes scarce during the dry season, UNMISS said.

Whether the reservoir will ultimately help reduce cattle-related violence remains to be seen, but its impact is already extending well beyond supplying water.

In a community long divided by competition over scarce resources, the project has brought farmers and herders together around a shared resource and fostered renewed hope that Rego can once again become a place people call home.

articles.reasoning: The article reports on a completed reservoir project in South Sudan that provides a sustainable water source, addressing a key driver of conflict between farmers and cattle keepers. This initiative promotes peace, community cooperation, and supports displaced populations returning home, thus having a broad positive social impact in a conflict-affected region.
articles.personality_title: New reservoir in South Sudan helps farmers and herders share water and peace
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In Terekeka county, South Sudan, dry land and past conflicts over water and grazing have made life hard for farmers and cattle keepers. Fighting over these scarce resources has caused many problems and even forced some people to leave their homes.

**What happened** – The United Nations peacekeeping mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) built a new artificial lake, or reservoir, to provide fresh water to the area. The project was finished in just one month and includes an underground water source that keeps the reservoir full even during dry seasons. Local communities helped build roads and clear the site, showing strong cooperation.

**Impact** – This reservoir gives farmers a steady water supply for their crops and means herders don’t need to bring their cattle onto farms looking for water. This helps reduce fights between the two groups. Some displaced people have already started returning home, encouraged by the new water and peace. The project has brought the communities closer and created hope for a better future.

**What's next step** – The community will continue to use and care for the reservoir. If successful, this model of sharing water could help other areas with similar problems. People hope that over time, the reservoir will lower tensions and support lasting peace between farmers and herders.

**One-sentence takeaway** – A new water reservoir in South Sudan is helping farmers and cattle herders share resources, reduce conflict, and rebuild their community together.
articles.personality_title_fr: Un nouveau réservoir au Soudan du Sud aide agriculteurs et éleveurs à partager l'eau et la paix
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Dans le comté de Terekeka au Soudan du Sud, la sécheresse et les conflits liés à l'eau et aux pâturages rendent la vie difficile pour les agriculteurs et les éleveurs. Ces disputes ont même forcé certaines personnes à quitter leur foyer.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – La mission de maintien de la paix des Nations Unies au Soudan du Sud (UNMISS) a construit un nouveau lac artificiel, ou réservoir, pour fournir de l'eau douce à la région. Le projet a été achevé en un mois seulement et comprend une source d'eau souterraine qui maintient le réservoir rempli même en saison sèche. Les communautés locales ont aidé à construire des routes et à nettoyer le site, montrant une forte coopération.

**Impact** – Ce réservoir offre aux agriculteurs un approvisionnement régulier en eau pour leurs cultures et évite aux éleveurs de faire paître leur bétail sur les terres agricoles. Cela réduit les conflits entre les deux groupes. Certaines personnes déplacées ont déjà commencé à rentrer chez elles, encouragées par cette nouvelle eau et la paix retrouvée. Le projet a rapproché les communautés et créé un espoir pour un avenir meilleur.

**Prochaine étape** – La communauté continuera à utiliser et entretenir le réservoir. Si le projet réussit, ce modèle de partage de l'eau pourrait être reproduit dans d'autres régions ayant des problèmes similaires. On espère qu'avec le temps, le réservoir réduira les tensions et soutiendra une paix durable entre agriculteurs et éleveurs.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Un nouveau réservoir d'eau au Soudan du Sud aide agriculteurs et éleveurs à partager les ressources, réduire les conflits et reconstruire leur communauté ensemble.
articles.personality_title_es: Nuevo embalse en Sudán del Sur ayuda a agricultores y ganaderos a compartir agua y paz
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En el condado de Terekeka, Sudán del Sur, la sequía y los conflictos por el agua y los pastos han dificultado la vida de agricultores y ganaderos. Estas peleas incluso han obligado a algunas personas a abandonar sus hogares.

**Qué pasó** – La misión de mantenimiento de la paz de la ONU en Sudán del Sur (UNMISS) construyó un nuevo lago artificial, o embalse, para proporcionar agua fresca a la zona. El proyecto se completó en solo un mes e incluye una fuente de agua subterránea que mantiene el embalse lleno incluso en la estación seca. Las comunidades locales ayudaron a construir caminos y limpiar el lugar, mostrando una fuerte cooperación.

**Impacto** – Este embalse ofrece a los agricultores un suministro constante de agua para sus cultivos y evita que los ganaderos lleven su ganado a las tierras de cultivo en busca de agua. Esto ayuda a reducir los conflictos entre ambos grupos. Algunas personas desplazadas ya han comenzado a regresar a sus hogares, animadas por esta nueva agua y la paz. El proyecto ha unido a las comunidades y creado esperanza para un futuro mejor.

**Próximo paso** – La comunidad seguirá usando y cuidando el embalse. Si tiene éxito, este modelo de compartir agua podría ayudar a otras zonas con problemas similares. Se espera que con el tiempo, el embalse disminuya las tensiones y apoye una paz duradera entre agricultores y ganaderos.

**Resumen en una frase** – Un nuevo embalse en Sudán del Sur está ayudando a agricultores y ganaderos a compartir recursos, reducir conflictos y reconstruir su comunidad juntos.

articles.title: The £70 refund letter that isn't a scam
articles.summary: About one million people - mostly women - are owed pension tax relief and will be contacted by HMRC.
articles.content:
You may be among the one million people, mostly women, who will receive letters explaining how you are eligible for top-up payments - and it's not a scam.

Those entitled are low earners who have missed out on the money because of the way the pension they pay into is administered.

HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will write to people over the next few months, explaining how to receive the payment. Typically they will be due £70, but that may vary considerably depending on their circumstances.

Anyone eligible - the vast majority of whom will be of working age rather than pensioners - will be contacted automatically. But, if you receive a letter, there are various checks you can do to ensure the letter is genuine so you don't get hoodwinked.
articles.reasoning: The article reports a significant government action to refund pension tax relief to about one million people, mostly women, correcting a financial oversight and providing tangible economic benefit to a large group, thereby improving financial justice and equity.
articles.personality_title: HMRC to refund £70 pension tax relief to one million people
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Many low earners, mostly women, missed out on pension tax relief payments due to how their pension contributions were handled.

**What happened** – HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will send letters in the next few months to about one million people, explaining how they can claim a pension tax refund. Most will receive around £70, but amounts may differ depending on individual cases.

**Impact** – This refund corrects a financial mistake affecting mostly working-age people, mainly women, ensuring they receive money they were owed. It helps make pension tax rules fairer and supports people who may have missed out on extra income.

**What's next step** – People who get the letter will be guided on how to claim their payment safely. HMRC advises checking the letter’s authenticity to avoid scams. This process will continue as letters are sent out over the coming months.

**One-sentence takeaway** – HMRC is returning pension tax relief money to one million eligible people, mainly women, correcting past payment errors and providing them with owed funds.
articles.personality_title_fr: HMRC rembourse 70 £ de crédit d'impôt retraite à un million de personnes
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – De nombreux petits salariés, principalement des femmes, n'ont pas reçu des crédits d'impôt retraite à cause de la façon dont leurs cotisations ont été gérées.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) enverra dans les prochains mois des lettres à environ un million de personnes, expliquant comment réclamer un remboursement d'impôt sur la retraite. La plupart recevront environ 70 £, mais le montant peut varier selon les cas.

**Impact** – Ce remboursement corrige une erreur financière qui touchait surtout des personnes en âge de travailler, principalement des femmes, en leur restituant l'argent qui leur était dû. Cela rend les règles d'imposition des retraites plus justes et aide ceux qui ont manqué ces revenus.

**Prochaine étape** – Les personnes recevant la lettre seront guidées pour réclamer leur paiement en toute sécurité. HMRC recommande de vérifier l'authenticité de la lettre pour éviter les arnaques. L'envoi des lettres se poursuivra dans les mois à venir.

**Une phrase clé** – HMRC rembourse les crédits d'impôt retraite à un million de bénéficiaires, surtout des femmes, rectifiant des erreurs passées et leur rendant l'argent dû.
articles.personality_title_es: HMRC devolverá 70 £ de alivio fiscal de pensiones a un millón de personas
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Muchas personas con bajos ingresos, principalmente mujeres, no recibieron pagos de alivio fiscal para pensiones debido a cómo se manejaron sus contribuciones.

**Qué pasó** – HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) enviará cartas en los próximos meses a cerca de un millón de personas, explicando cómo pueden reclamar un reembolso de impuestos de pensiones. La mayoría recibirá alrededor de 70 £, aunque la cantidad puede variar según cada caso.

**Impacto** – Este reembolso corrige un error financiero que afectó principalmente a personas en edad laboral, en su mayoría mujeres, asegurando que reciban el dinero que se les debía. Esto hace que las reglas fiscales sobre pensiones sean más justas y ayuda a quienes no recibieron ingresos adicionales.

**Próximo paso** – Las personas que reciban la carta serán guiadas para reclamar su pago de forma segura. HMRC recomienda verificar la autenticidad de la carta para evitar estafas. El envío de cartas continuará en los próximos meses.

**Una frase clave** – HMRC está devolviendo dinero de alivio fiscal de pensiones a un millón de personas elegibles, principalmente mujeres, corrigiendo errores pasados y entregándoles fondos que les corresponden.
